newsitem.title: USA: Exxon sees earlier Sakhalin production start.
newsitem.headline: Exxon sees earlier Sakhalin production start.

text.p: Exxon Corp anticipates the Sakhalin I Consortium will start-up production shortly after the turn of the century, spokesman Ed Burwell said Thursday.

He was commenting on a statement released in Tokyo by the consortium's Japanese partner, Sakhalin Oil Development Cooperation Corp, saying the project is likely to start pumping oil around 2001-1002, earlier than the initial schedule of around 2004.
"We'd prefer to not name a year," Burwell said.

The company's Exxon Neftegas Ltd subsidiary is operator of the Sakhalin I Consortium and has a 30 percent interest, as does SODECO. Two Russian companies, Sakhalinmorneftegas-Shelf and Rosneft-Sakhalin have a 23 and 17 percent interest, respectively.
Exxon noted field work was initiated on the first part of a $200-$300 million resource appraisal program after the production sharing agreement was declared effective in June.
Burwell said "in exxcess of $140 million" of that will be spent in 1997.
The company said 3D seismic data has been gathered over the Arkutun-Dagi field, offshore Sakhalin Island.
The group completed "the first well to be drilled under a PSA in Russia, the Dagi-5," in the Arkutun-Dagi field.

Drilled to a depth of 2,500 meters (8,200 feet), the well was completed on October 14, confirming oil reserves in the central portion of the field. The core samples and other data from the well are currently being analyzed.
Design studies for the first phase of development of the Arkutun-Dagi field also are being planned for 1997.
Under consideration is a 40-slot, ice-resistant platform in about 45 meters (150 feet) of water to develop oil reserves in the central portion of the Arkutun-Dagi field, Exxon said.

The first phase development also will include provisions for oil export and domestic oil sales. "The consortium's objective is to establish commercial oil production from this first phase as soon as prudently possible," the statement said.

During 1997, Exxon said, the consortium plans to drill three additional appraisal wells in the Arkutun-Dagi field and acquire additional 3D seismic on Chayvo, a second offshore field in the Sakhalin I area.

Two of the wells will be drilled with the Rosneft-Sakhalinmorneftegas (SMNG) OKHA jack-up rig that is under contract to the Consortium, Exxon said. SMNG also will supply work boats to support the drilling effort.
A rig to drill the third well will be contracted separately, the company said. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
